original_record.question:
We link rings together as shown in the figure below; the length of the chain is $1.7 \mathrm{~m}$. How many rings are there?
<image1>

inventory.image1: schematic interlinked circular annuli: two complete first rings, left half of third, ellipsis, right half of penultimate, complete last; first ring inner/outer radius leaders2cm/3cm; full chain1.7m dimension with solid endpoint connectors and dashed parallel line
inventory.native_geometry: outer radius3,inner2,adjacent displayed center spacing4; opaque native annular half-sectors and exact circular edges implement source over/under crossings; no bitmap clipping
inventory.source_style_change: overall chain dimension uses protocol dashed parallel line plus two solid connectors, no arrows, labels remain source text

answer_verification.method: Annulus thickness3-2=1cm. As depicted, the first ring contributes outside diameter6cm and each additional interlocked ring contributes inside diameter4cm. Hence6+4(n-1)=170 and n=42. Ellipsis compresses undisplayed links; its display-coordinate separation is not used as physical length.
